scripts.//test: VERIFY_SWEEP and --concurrency=1 are a matched pair: turbo runs each workspace's test suite one at a time instead of overlapping them, and VERIFY_SWEEP tells the vitest configs (declared as passThroughEnv in turbo.json — turbo runs in strict env mode) to hold their fork pools at the low-spec floor for the duration instead of the wider pool a standalone `pnpm test:frontend` may use. Backend jest is pinned separately (apps/backend/jest.config.cjs, maxWorkers: 2). Co-scheduling several full-width pools at once mostly bought heat and memory pressure rather than throughput, since the suites contend for the same cores; running them sequentially trades wall time for a low, predictable ceiling that behaves the same on every machine. NOTE the reach of --concurrency: it bounds EVERY task in the run, not just the test tasks, so the `^build` fan-in this task depends on is serialized too. Inside `pnpm verify` that costs nothing — `pnpm build` has already run and turbo replays it from cache — but a cold-cache standalone `pnpm test` builds the workspace packages one at a time before the first suite starts. Run `pnpm build` first if that matters; deliberately NOT chained in here, because `turbo run build` would additionally build the apps themselves, which the test graph does not need.
scripts.//verify: `smoke:dist` runs straight after the build because `build` only proves tsc emitted files, not that Node can load them — see apps/backend/scripts/dist-boot-guard.mjs. It needs the backend's workspace deps built too, hence the topological `@repo/backend...` filter in verify:backend. `smoke:tsnode` covers the opposite blind spot: the ts-node dev/seed/openapi pipeline resolves modules with the node10 resolver, which no other gate exercises — see apps/backend/scripts/tsnode-boot-guard.cjs. `check:drift` (packages/services/scripts/check-client-drift.ts) runs right after it because it exercises that same ts-node openapi:extract entry point — it fails when a backend contract change shipped without the matching `pnpm gen:client`, which is a mismatch between two workspaces that no single-package verify would otherwise catch, so it is in verify:backend too: a backend contract change is exactly what trips it, and the person running verify:backend is the one most likely to have caused it. On weaker machines, `TURBO_CONCURRENCY=2 pnpm verify` throttles how many workspace tasks each turbo phase runs at once (the test task's explicit --concurrency=1 still wins for that phase).
scripts.verify: pnpm --filter @repo/backend prisma:lint && pnpm lint && pnpm build && pnpm --filter @repo/backend smoke:dist && pnpm --filter @repo/backend smoke:tsnode && pnpm --filter @repo/services check:drift && pnpm typecheck && pnpm test
scripts.verify:backend: pnpm --filter @repo/backend prisma:lint && pnpm --filter @repo/backend lint && pnpm --filter "@repo/backend..." build && pnpm --filter @repo/backend smoke:dist && pnpm --filter @repo/backend smoke:tsnode && pnpm --filter @repo/services check:drift && pnpm --filter @repo/backend typecheck && pnpm --filter @repo/backend test
scripts.verify:frontend: pnpm --filter @repo/frontend lint && pnpm --filter @repo/frontend build && pnpm --filter @repo/frontend typecheck && pnpm --filter @repo/frontend test
